Which Prop Firms Allow Options Trading in 2026?

The prop trading landscape is evolving. As we move through 2026, one of the most pressing questions among active traders is: which prop firms actually allow options trading, and under what conditions?

This isn’t just about finding funding. It’s about unlocking entire new playbooks for your trading style, and tapping into markets that most retail accounts can’t access at scale. Getting funded for options trading by a reputable prop firm in 2026 can mean the difference between plateauing with limited capital or scaling your edge onto a larger stage.

This comprehensive guide will benchmark the latest offerings. We’ll reveal which firms you can trust for options trading, how those models work, and, crucially, what specific risk, profit split, and evaluation rules you should expect as an aspiring funded options trader.

If you’re asking, “Where can I trade options with prop firm capital in 2026?”, you’re in the right place.

---

The Modern Prop Firm: Funding Your Options Trading Ambitions

Prop firms, or proprietary trading firms, partner with skilled traders by providing them access to firm-owned capital. Profits are then split, often handsomely, with the trader. Over the last ten years, this model boomed in forex and futures, and only recently have more firms welcomed verified, funded options trading.

But be careful: not all prop firms offer the same flexibility, or the same product set, for options.

Why? Options contracts are complex, and risk oversight is trickier for a firm than, say, with simple spot forex. As a result, only a handful of firms support outright options trading, while many offer related exposures (e.g., CFDs on underlying stocks or indices) that are not true listed options.

A true options-prop firm settles trades on regulated options markets (like CBOE, CME, Eurex) and allows you to undertake everything from covered calls to complex spreads, with real-time risk controls.

If you’re looking to make money trading options with prop firm capital, make sure you’re clear: you need a firm that offers actual options execution and supports the strategies you plan to trade. Spot or CFD-only prop firms simply won’t deliver what you need for multi-leg and volatility-based trades.

---

How Prop Firms Structure Options Trading in 2026

Most funded trader programs for options trading in 2026 share a core model:

  • You apply and “audition” via a trading evaluation (simulated or real capital)
  • If you hit profit and risk targets, you’re funded with a live account
  • You trade options, splitting profits (typically 70 to 95%) with the firm

The main differences come in the details:

  • Which exchanges and products are supported? (e.g. US listed options, Europe, Asia)
  • Account funding size (ranging from $10,000 up to $1 million equivalent, depending on the firm and your results)
  • How risk is managed: static vs rolling drawdowns, per-trade risk limits, margin calls
  • What’s allowed: news trading, hedging, automated strategies, exotic spreads

The prop firm options trading ecosystem in 2026 is more accommodating than ever, yet remains intensely selective. Passing the evaluation is a real hurdle, but with options-specific experience and modern risk controls, it’s absolutely within reach for serious traders.

Key Criteria: Choosing the Best Options Trading Prop Firm

Choosing where to attempt your evaluation (or challenge) requires more than a price comparison. Here’s what expert options traders look for in 2026:

1. Product Access & Platforms

Do they offer direct, listed options trading (not just CFDs)? Which venues can you access? For instance, some firms only support US equity options, while others will open Eurex or CME contracts. Best-in-class firms provide multi-venue access, especially useful if you trade index/volatility options worldwide.

Equally important, what is the platform? MT4 or cTrader may suffice for spot FX, but serious options traders need dedicated options software (think Thinkorswim, Interactive Brokers, Tradestation, or access through DMA platforms). Always confirm this before committing.

2. Trading Rules & Flexibility

Are multi-leg strategies allowed? What about earnings/news trading, automated options strategies, or even hedging across positions? Some firms restrict accounts to outright calls and puts, while the best allow iron condors, vertical spreads, ratio writing, and more.

Do the drawdown and risk rules translate well to the high-volatility world of options? A fixed 5% daily max loss may sound fair, but if it’s based on gross rather than net portfolio exposure, sophisticated spreads could be unintentionally penalized. Check for rules specific to options margining, not just spot/cash drawdown.

3. Capital Sizes & Ramp-Up

What is the minimum and maximum fund size on offer? Some options-focused firms start accounts at $10,000, while others boast $100,000 or even $500,000 initial accounts for those who pass an advanced evaluation. Favor firms that support scaling up as you prove consistency, so your growth is not capped.

Firms like TradersYard offer account sizes up to $500,000 and allow scaling post-payout for FX/CFD, view account sizes.

4. Profit Splits & Payout Frequency

Options setups take time to mature and unwind. Look for firms with a fair split (80 to 95% to the trader is best) and fast, reliable payouts, ideally within 24-48 hours via crypto or bank transfer. This ensures you’re incentivized, not hamstrung by bureaucracy.

5. Reputation, Oversight, and E.U. Compliance

This is non-negotiable in 2026. Only trust options prop firms with proven track records, regulated oversight where applicable, and near-instant support. EU-compliant, local-country-based firms offer critical consumer protections absent in offshore “no-name” shops.

Prop Firms That Allow Options Trading: 2026 Reality Check

Which Prop Firms Actually Offer Options in 2026?

Based on extensive industry research, comparison sites, and direct trader reviews, here’s where reputable prop firms stand on options:

  • True options trading remains rare in the prop firm world. Most global mega-firms focus on FX, indices, futures, and spot commodities. Only a handful support actual options, most others offer only underlying assets, not listed derivatives contracts.
  • Leading US and European “remote” prop firms like SMB Capital, Maverick Trading, and T3 Trading Group continue to offer options funding on homegrown software, but require rigorous interviews and often upfront ‘risk deposit’ or capital commitment.
  • Several new, “challenge-based” funding firms have trialed options markets, but often revert to simulated environments or restrict eligible strategies.
  • Inspection of official lists for 2026 shows few truly global, no-deposit prop firms supporting non-US residents for options, even as CFD and forex funding surges worldwide.

For serious options traders, vet every single detail before joining an evaluation or paying a fee. Look up reviews, ask for a product demonstration, never assume “options” means you have full flexibility.

A Detailed Look at Risk Controls, Evaluation, and Unique Insights

Not all prop firm evaluation programs handle options risk the same way. Here are some expert-only insights for 2026 options prop firm selection:

The Depth of Real-Time Risk

The single biggest difference between a good options prop desk and a “challenge” generic firm is real-time margin and risk calculation.

  • Professional options-focused shops use live risk engines to calculate total portfolio Greeks (Delta, Gamma, Vega, Theta) across all positions, adjusting net margin, drawdown, and liquidation triggers in real time.
  • Some retail-funded prop models simply check account equity and P&L at day’s end, fine for spot, totally inadequate for complex option spreads.

Why does this matter? If your prop firm can’t monitor your net exposure as you roll through multi-leg structures or adjust for upcoming expiries or dividends, a sharp volatility move could trigger forced liquidation of even risk-neutral spreads, destroying your profitability (and potentially the firm’s capital too).

Before joining a prop firm to trade options, demand a demonstration of risk controls. Ask:

  • How do they calculate drawdown for opposing or hedged legs?
  • How is early assignment risk managed?
  • What margin offsets do they support for spreads, and do they apply span margining like real exchanges?

If you can’t get transparent answers, walk away.

One-Step Evaluation vs Multi-Stage Filters

The most trader-friendly prop options programs (rare, but growing by 2026) use one-step evaluations that reflect real trading scenarios, a single phase, with fixed rules and live profit/risk targets.

Beware multi-phase programs with “paper trading only” first stages, as those rarely allow the complex execution or fills that live options trading relies on. Similarly, avoid any firm with daily loss limits that don’t account for options expiry or Greek decay, as these rules can accidentally penalize neutral strategies.

Platforms like TradersYard excel in one-step, low-friction evaluations for FX/CFD, though do not offer direct options as of 2026.

Options Liquidity, Execution, and Slippage Rules

Even among firms that allow options trading, the real test is order execution:

  • Can you execute spreads in a single ticket, or do you have to leg in?
  • What is their policy on partial fills, wide bid/asks, or illiquid strikes?
  • Are all exchange fees transparently passed to the trader, or hidden in conversion/spread?

Savvy traders in 2026 will recognize that many “options prop” firms restrict to deep-in-the-money or near-the-money liquid contracts only. This works for some bread-and-butter income trades but fails for volatility arbitrage, calendar spreads, or custom tail hedges.

When evaluating firms, ask for an execution demo or live account reference before proceeding.

---

The Evolution of Options-Focused Prop Funds: Trends for 2026 and Beyond

Prop firm options trading is amid a period of genuine transformation. More exchange integration, AI-powered risk, and demand for multi-venue access are all reshaping trader options. The “challenge model” funding so common in forex is slowly spreading into listed derivatives, but it will never replace the value of desk apprenticeship and live mentorship from traditional prop shops.
